sanskrit_verse:
dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā ।
 catuṣprakāro 'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ ॥ BrhS_1,9.1 ॥
transliteration: dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā | catuṣprakāro 'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rthe vinirṇayaḥ || BrhS_1,9.1 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In matters of doubt, resolution arises through fourfold means: by Dharma, by conduct, by character, and by the command of the King.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma
Royal decree resolves when lower pramāṇas conflict
supreme_court_application: The Supreme Court shall first assess alignment with Dharma. If ambiguity remains, evaluate personal conduct and public character. Only then apply royal edict where necessary. Responsibility is determined by consciousness clarity, not coercive force.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Resolution follows sequential manifestation: Dharma as foundation, conduct as expression, character as root, and royal will as final stabilizer. No punitive intent is entertained; all actions aim at realigning consciousness to its innate integrity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate dharmic inquiry into root misalignment
Assign completion process based on individual capacity
Reintegrate actor via supervised alignment practices
Verify restoration through witnessed conduct consistency
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. Dharma prevails through consciousness restoration. Justice serves reintegration alone. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the ultimate judge.
